title: Automated Production of Human Stem Cell Derived Liver Spheres
author: Meseguer-Ripolles, Kasarinaite, et al.
materials: This step describes how to prepare the 96-well plate Gri3D® for cell seeding. Each well of a 96-well plate Gri3D contains a Polyethylene glycol (PEG)- hydrogel with 73 micromolds of 500 μM of diameter. Upon adding a single-cell suspension in the wells, cells will be deposited into the micromolds by gravity where they will start to self-assemble into spheroids. Each well of the Gri3D plates, contains a feeder cavity or well which can be used for media change to reduce spheroid disruption (Figure 1A). Wells need to be washed prior spheroid formation to remove shipping buffer. By using automatic liquid handling systems, semi-automation of this process can be achieved. For this protocol we use both Multidop (Thermofisher) and Viaflo (Integra) systems. First, the multidrop is a high-speed dispenser compatible with 6- to 1536-well plates, it works by dispensing specific volumes into the wells in a column-based manner using dispensing cassettes which can vary depending on the volume to dispense, in our protocol we use standard dispensing cassettes. The Viaflo is a handheld 24, 96 or 384 channel programmable pipette that allows an increase throughput when working with multi-well plates. The Viaflo can be used with either a two- or three-plate station. The usage of the three-plate station minimizes the risk of contamination by reducing the need of changing plates when working under sterile conditions.61.Place the 96-well plate Gri3D® into one of the plate holders of a three station Viaflo with a 96 well head. Place the plate with the A1 well facing the top left, the microwells or feeder wells should be facing left at this position (Figure 1A). Place a 96-deep well plate into the next position of the station and use it as a waste.62.Prepare a 96-deep well plate with 900 μL of DPBS per well for Gri3D® plate to be prepared. This will serve as a reservoir of DPBS to wash three times the Gri3D® plates to prepare them for cell culture. Place the deep well plate with DPBS into the last Viaflo station available.Note: The use of a multidrop with a standard cassette to dispense the DPBS into the deep well can reduce time and variability.63.Position the Viaflo head in the Gri3D® plate position, move the pin of the plate holder to the left to work in a 384-well plate mode. This mode should align the tips with the microwell of the 96-well plate Gri3D®.64.To remove all the shipment buffer from the wells, aspirate 300 μL from the feeder well. Move the Viaflo head into the central position (Figure 1B) where the waste deep-well plate for waste is placed. Pin back to center to work in a 96-well plate mode and dispense the liquid into the waste plate.65.Move the plate station to the right for the Viaflo to access the plate with DPBS. Aspirate 250 μL. Move the plate station to the right and move the pin to the left to work in a 384-well plate mode. Place the tips into the feeder well and dispense the 250 μL into the feeder well. Mix up and down 100 μL five times to ensure any reminder of the buffer from the Gri3D® plate is mixed with the DPBS.66.This process is considered a wash, repeat it two more times to ensure full removal of the Gri3D® plate.Note: The volume DPBS dispensed into the deep-well should cover the three washes.67.After the last wash, leave the DPBS into the plate and place it into the incubator at 37°C/5% CO2 to warm up the hydrogel from Gri3D® plate until the cell suspension for liver sphere aggregation is prepared.Figure 1Schematic representation of the sphere production pipeline(A) Schematic representation of a well of a Gri3D_ plate.(B) Suggested use of the Viaflo plate station. Position 1 – for the 96-well plate Gri3D_ with the microwells (feeder wells) facing left. Position 2 - for a 96- deep well plate for the waste collection. Position 3 – for the ‘V’-shape plate with the cell suspension. Position 4 – for accessing the feeder well by moving the pin to the left.

steps.title: Thaw and dilute LN‑521
steps.instruction: Thaw a 100 µg/mL stock vial of recombinant laminin‑521 (LN‑521) at 4 °C overnight (10–12 h). Dilute the thawed LN‑521 in ice‑cold 1× DPBS (with Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺) to a final concentration of 5 µg/mL.

steps.title: Coat plates with LN‑521
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL of the 5 µg/mL LN‑521 solution to each well of a 6‑well plate (or 5 mL to each 55 cm² petri dish) ensuring the entire surface is covered.

steps.title: Incubate and store coated plates
steps.instruction: Incubate the coated plates or dishes at 37 °C/5 % CO₂ for 2 h (or at 4 °C overnight, 10–12 h). After coating, store plates at 4 °C on a flat surface, seal with parafilm to prevent evaporation, and use within two weeks.

steps.title: Warm coated plates before use
steps.instruction: Warm the coated plate/dish by placing it in a 37 °C/5 % CO₂ incubator for 30 min or at room temperature (15–21 °C) for 2 h. To further reduce evaporation, add an extra 1 mL of 1× DPBS (with Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺) and keep the plate sealed.

steps.title: Prepare stem cell maintenance medium
steps.instruction: Add 100 mL mTeSR1™ 5× supplement to 400 mL mTeSR1™ basal medium to obtain complete stem cell medium.

substeps.instruction: Endoderm differentiation medium: to 500 mL RPMI‑1640 add 1 % penicillin‑streptomycin and 1× B27 supplement.

Hepatic progenitor differentiation medium: mix 400 mL KO‑DMEM, 100 mL KOSR serum replacement, 1 % non‑essential amino acids, 1 % DMSO, 1 % penicillin‑streptomycin, 0.5 % GlutaMAX, and 0.2 % β‑mercaptoethanol.
Hepatocyte maturation medium: combine 500 mL Hepato‑ZYME, 10 µM hydrocortisone 21‑hemisuccinate sodium salt (HCC), 1 % penicillin‑streptomycin, and 1 % GlutaMAX.
Mesoderm priming N2B27: mix 250 mL DMEM/F12, 250 mL CTS Neurobasal, 2.5 mL GlutaMAX (100×), 10 mL CTS B27, 5 mL CTS N2, and 0.5 mL β‑mercaptoethanol.
Reconstitute StemPro‑34 SFM according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Prepare hepatic stellate cell medium
steps.instruction: Combine 57 % DMEM low glucose, 40 % MCDB‑201 (water), 0.25× linoleic‑acid‑BSA, 0.25× insulin‑transferrin‑selenium, 1 % penicillin‑streptomycin, 1 × 10⁻⁴ M L‑ascorbic acid, 2.5 µM dexamethasone, and 50 µM β‑mercaptoethanol.

steps.title: Prepare liver sphere culture medium
steps.instruction: Mix William’s E medium and SFM‑Endothelial medium 1:1, then add 5 % serum replacement, 1 % GlutaMAX, and 1 % penicillin‑streptomycin.

steps.title: Set up Gri3D® plate washing station
steps.instruction: Arrange the Viaflo three‑station holder: position 1 – 96‑well Gri3D® plate (A1 top‑left, microwells facing left); position 2 – 96‑deep‑well plate for waste; position 3 – 96‑deep‑well plate containing 900 µL DPBS per well (wash reservoir). Use a Multidrop with a standard cassette to dispense DPBS into the deep‑well reservoir if desired.

steps.title: Wash Gri3D® plate to remove shipping buffer

substeps.instruction: Aspirate 300 µL from the feeder well of the Gri3D® plate and dispense into the waste deep‑well plate.
Aspirate 250 µL DPBS from the reservoir plate, move the Viaflo pin to 384‑well mode, place tips into the feeder well, and dispense the 250 µL DPBS into the feeder well.
Mix up‑and‑down 100 µL five times to ensure residual buffer is released into the DPBS.
Repeat the aspirate‑dispense‑mix cycle two more times for a total of three washes, ensuring the DPBS volume in the reservoir covers all washes.

steps.title: Warm washed Gri3D® plate before seeding
steps.instruction: After the final wash, leave the DPBS in the plate and incubate at 37 °C/5 % CO₂ until the cell suspension for liver‑sphere aggregation is ready.
